title: Shortstack SDK playground checklist and pairing notes
content:
Context and intent:

This is a compact, hands-on checklist + pairing script for a 30–45 minute in-person / remote workshop we can run with new SDK adopters or internal engineers who need a no-friction first loop into Redwood SDK + local playground. Focus: confidence (first success), clear failure modes, and measurable telemetry hooks so we can iterate on docs and infra.

Audience:
- Backend/frontend engineers who need a fast path to a working sample app and one small feature.
- Solutions engineers running workshops for customers.

Goals (outcomes after the session):
- Participant runs the local playground and issues a single generate + embedding call.
- Participant understands how to switch models / toggle streaming / enable a simple cache.
- Pairing lead captures 3 friction points and a telemetry artifact.

Prep (for host):
- Laptop with Node 18+ and Python 3.11 installed.
- Local env template repo checked out: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-playground (branch: shortstack-demo).
- Docker optional: docker up to speed for Windows/mac parity.
- An API key stub: use test/demo key (do not use prod credentials).
- Quicklinks: PR-489, Confluence shortstack page, JIRA-219.

Quick checklist (15–25 minutes):
1) Clone and install (ask participant to run with you):
   - git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/sdk-playground.git -b shortstack-demo
   - cd shortstack-demo && npm ci   # or pip install -r requirements.txt for python runner
2) Copy .env.template -> .env, insert demo key (KEY-DEMO-XXXX) and set REGION=us-west2
3) Start dev server: npm run dev (open localhost:5173) or python -m http.server 8000 for the static bundle
4) Run smoke calls from CLI: 
   - curl -X POST http://localhost:5173/api/generate -d '{"prompt":"Write a 2-line haiku about debugging"}'
   - curl -X POST http://localhost:5173/api/embedding -d '{"text":"redwood inference"}'
5) Observe the playground UI streaming response and the embedding vector printed in console.

Pairing script (what the host says / does):
- 0–2 min: Explain scope: "We will get a minimal feature working end-to-end: SDK call -> model response -> simple telemetry. If we get blocked, we'll swap to a recorded demo to keep momentum."
- 2–10 min: Walk through clone/install. Stop and verify dev tooling.
- 10–20 min: Walk participant through editing a single file: routes/api/generate.js (or app/main.py). Explain where the SDK client is instantiated and where to change model name / streaming flag.
- 20–30 min: Run the request together, show token-level timing in the dev console (we instrument timing in sdk-client.debug()).
- 30–45 min: Add one small change: enable prefix caching (flip CACHE_PREFIX=true) and re-run the same prompt to show latency improvement. Discuss tradeoffs briefly.

Key files and quick notes for hosts:
- routes/api/generate.js: minimal handler, lots of commented 'swap-in' patterns for streaming vs batch
- lib/sdk-client.js: one place to swap credentials, tag telemetry events, and enable the debug timing hook
- playground/static/prompts.md: curated set of short prompts for demos (keep it < 6 prompts)

Telemetry & observability hooks (must be captured during pairing):
- Capture these three logs during each session: sdk-init-timestamp, request-latency-ms, tokens-generated-count.
- In the sample app we emit these to console and to a local file telemetry/sessions.log so hosts can attach the log to the pairing ticket.
- Ask participant to paste a single request id into the Confluence shortstack page after the session.

Smoke tests to run if something breaks:
- Is the dev server listening? curl localhost:5173/__health -> 200 {"ok":true}
- Invalid key => server returns 401 with clear error payload. If you see 500, escalate (likely mismatch in env or missing dependency).
- Model mismatch key: SDK should respond with 422 with list of supported model slugs.

Common friction we expect and quick fixes:
- Windows firewall blocks local port -> switch to a remote shared sandbox or run with host's container.
- Slow installs (CI/registry) -> have a cached node_modules tarball ready.
- Streaming not appearing -> confirm SSE polyfill (older browsers) and check Content-Type header.

Mini exercises (optional, 10–15 min extra):
- Swap the model to a smaller quantized variant and re-run prompt; note token/time delta.
- Add a second request that uses the embedding result to rerank two canned answers (demo reranking pipeline).
- Toggle TELEMETRY=false and discuss consequences for observability.

Capture template (host to fill during session):
- participant: __________________
- time started: __________________
- success (Y/N): __
- friction notes (top 3): __, __, __
- telemetry log path: telemetry/sessions.log (last entry id: __)
- follow-up ticket if any: JIRA-____

Troubleshooting snippets (for host):
- Recreate env quickly: rm -rf node_modules && npm ci --prefer-offline --no-audit
- Run with debug logging: NODE_DEBUG=sdk-client npm run dev
- Fallback recorded demo: recorded-demo/shortstack-20250208.mp4 (host can share if participant is stuck)

Design notes / why this is shortstack vs full bootcamp:
- Target short timeboxed sessions for customers who only want a quick proof of integration or for internal teams doing pre-sales demos.
- Emphasis on capturing telemetry and failure modes rather than covering every API surface.

Open questions / TODOs (to iterate on after running 10 sessions):
- Do we need a lighter Windows-specific installer? (ticket: JIRA-DEVEXP-332)
- Should we add an embeddable iframe walkthrough to avoid local env pain? (pro/con list needed)
- Can we standardize the sample key rotation to avoid leaked demo keys in logs?

Notes to self (hosting tips):
- Keep the session within 45 minutes. If it drifts, pivot to recorded demo and schedule follow-up.
- Encourage participants to change one thing — small wins stick.
- Ask them to try the sample prompt again after enabling cache; the timing difference is the most convincing datapoint.

End of doc.

- 2025-02-10: initial sketch by Aisha Patel
